rationale: This is a largely cosmetic recombination of the archive's "Cash-Share-Verified Core Margin" (identical DELTA(che/act,1) leg) with a lagged profitability rank and MIN instead of MUL, and lagging the profit leg only makes the signal staler without adding a distinct economic mechanism.

It replicates the structure of the already-successful "Cash-Covered Operating Profit" with a much narrower and lumpier denominator, and che/(che+txp) saturates near 1 for the large fraction of firms with negligible taxes payable, so the second leg will be near-degenerate noise rather than a real tax-settlement-capacity measure.

The level-based reformulation of the debt-interest gap is a defensible substantive departure from the archive's change-based version with internally consistent signs, though the gap is likely dominated by debt-maturity mix and credit quality (cheap debt, low rates) rather than any concealed financing burden.

The "new historical low in noncash-working-capital intensity" leg is a genuinely different functional form from the archive's trend version and the construction matches the stated hypothesis, but it remains a within-family refinement whose incremental information over the existing trend signal may be small.

Internally consistent and pairs a distinct profit source (SG&A intensity change) with a cash-coverage change rather than re-using the same profitability leg, though it is a change-on-change double sort that will be noisy and thematically close to the archive's cash-verification cluster.

The second leg is essentially a monotone transform of net non-cash working capital scaled to (0,1), so the signal largely rediscovers the well-known net-operating-assets/working-capital accrual anomaly, and its stated direction directly contradicts the archive's own "Supplier-Independent Gross Profit" premise that heavier reliance on operating liabilities degrades profit quality.
